title: Con Edison Thanks Crews Mobilizing Ahead of Thanksgiving Coastal Storm
summary: Company Urges Public to Stay Safe and Avoid Downed Wires
body_markdown:
## How to Report an Outage


Customers can report outages and check service restoration status at conEd.com/reportoutage, with Con Edison’s mobile app for[iOS](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/con-edison/id654677047) or[Android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.coned.conedison&hl=en_US) devices or by calling 1-800-75-CONED (1-800-752-6633).


When reporting an outage, have your Con Edison account number available, if possible.


Customers who report outages will receive updates from Con Edison with their estimated restoration times as they become available.


Information on outages and restoration times is also available at the Con Edison[outage map](https://outagemap.coned.com/external/default.html) .


Customers can sign up for text alerts at coned.com/text.


## Storm Safety Tips


**Downed wires and equipment**


- Treat every downed wire as live. Don’t touch or move it with your hands or any object. Wires may be hidden by tree limbs, leaves, or water.
- Report downed wires to Con Edison or your local police department immediately.
- If a power line falls on your car, stay inside and wait for emergency personnel.
- Stay away from transformers that have fallen to the ground. They’re gray metal drums attached to wires and poles.
- For your safety, we may guard downed wires until crews make repairs. Our personnel may be in unmarked cars but will always have Con Edison identification.


**Preparation**


- Check that flashlights and battery-operated radios work, and keep extra batteries on hand.
- Charge cellphones and other mobile devices while you still have power.
- If the power goes out, turn off lights and appliances to help prevent overloaded circuits when service returns.
- Find more storm tips and preparation information at[conEd.com](https://www.coned.com/) .


**Flooding and generators**


- Use extreme caution when entering a flooded basement. Water contacting energized electrical equipment or appliances can cause serious injury or death.
- Follow the manufacturer’s instructions when installing and using a portable generator. Never plug it into a wall outlet or operate it indoors. Keep it outdoors and away from open windows and air-handling vents.


Customers can follow Con Edison on[X](https://twitter.com/conedison) or[Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/ConEdison) for general outage updates, safety tips and storm preparation information.


The company is in contact with New York City Emergency Management and the Westchester County Department of Emergency Services to coordinate storm response.
